issues.t: Plastic intake manifold cracks and dumps coolant
issues.sym: A sudden coolant leak at the front of the engine, often behind the alternator, steam from under the hood, a sweet smell, and the temperature gauge rising fast.
issues.why: The early 4.6L V8 used an all-plastic intake manifold with a plastic coolant passage across the front. That passage cracks with age and heat. CarComplaints rates it the worst Grand Marquis problem, and 1997 the worst year.
issues.next: If coolant pours out or the engine overheats, pull over and shut it off; driving on can warp the cylinder heads. Replace the manifold with the revised version that has an aluminum coolant crossover.

issues.t: Coolant seeping at the front of the intake manifold
issues.sym: Slow coolant loss, dried coolant crust at the front of the intake near the thermostat, or a faint sweet smell after driving.
issues.why: Later intake manifolds have an aluminum coolant crossover, but the plastic manifold and its seals can still leak where they meet, and some cars still develop cracks.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and look for crust at the front of the intake. A shop can pressure-test the system. A leaking manifold is usually replaced as a unit.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips, shifts erratically or fails
issues.sym: Slipping, a lost gear (often second), erratic shifting, hard engagement into first, or no movement at all.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic wears out with high mileage. Owners report clutch, band, solenoid and torque converter failures, often needing a rebuild.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Get a transmission diagnosis early, since solenoid or valve body faults are a smaller fix than a full rebuild.

issues.t: Misfire from a failed ignition coil
issues.sym: Rough running, a shaking idle, loss of power and a flashing or steady check engine light.
issues.why: Ignition coils are the most-reported repair in TrueDelta's Grand Marquis survey. They weaken with heat and age, and worn spark plugs and boots put extra strain on them.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read to find the cylinder. Replace the bad coil and check the plugs and boots. If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Clicking behind the dash or air stuck on hot or cold
issues.sym: A repeated clicking or ticking behind the dash, or air that stays hot or cold no matter where you set the temperature.
issues.why: The small electric motor that moves the heater blend door fails, or the door itself breaks. Repairs can require removing part of the dashboard.
issues.next: A shop can check whether the actuator or the door is at fault. Ask for an estimate first, because labor varies a lot.

issues.t: Worn ball joints and loose front end
issues.sym: Clunking or popping over bumps, vague or wandering steering, vibration, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: This heavy car wears out its front ball joints, shocks and stabilizer links. Owners often replace ball joints around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the front end checked for play at every tire rotation once the car is past 80,000 miles. A failed ball joint can let a wheel collapse, so do not wait.

issues.t: Loose steering from worn tie rods or steering linkage
issues.sym: Loose, wandering steering, play in the steering wheel, or clunks when turning.
issues.why: Tie rod ends and other steering linkage parts wear out on high-mileage cars, and owners report replacing tie rods, idler arms and Pitman arms.
issues.next: Have the steering linkage inspected and replace worn parts, then get an alignment.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure causes stalling or no start
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start, stalls, or loses power, especially at highway speeds or when hot.
issues.why: The electric fuel pump in the tank wears out. It is among the more common repairs owners report.
issues.next: A shop can check fuel pressure to confirm. If the car stalls while driving, get it off the road safely and have it towed.

issues.t: Gas pump keeps shutting off when refueling
issues.sym: The pump nozzle clicks off over and over when filling the tank, making it hard to fill up.
issues.why: The fuel tank vent or evaporative emissions parts become clogged or fail, so air cannot escape the tank while fueling.
issues.next: Have the evaporative emission system and tank vent checked. Some cars need a new vent valve or canister.

issues.t: Power window stops working from a broken regulator
issues.sym: A window will not go up or down, moves slowly, or makes a grinding or popping noise.
issues.why: The window regulator wears out or breaks.
issues.next: Replace the regulator, and the motor too if it is weak.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold
issues.sym: Warm air from the vents with the A/C on, a noisy compressor, or the A/C cycling on and off.
issues.why: The A/C compressor, hoses, seals and the accumulator are common failures as these cars age.
issues.next: Have the system leak-checked before recharging it. If the compressor failed, the accumulator and orifice tube should be replaced too.

issues.t: Heater core leak
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell inside the car, a foggy windshield, wet carpet on the passenger side, or coolant loss.
issues.why: The heater core inside the dash corrodes and leaks over time.
issues.next: Have it checked soon; coolant fumes are unpleasant and coolant loss can cause overheating. The repair is labor heavy because the core is behind the dash.

issues.t: Rear air suspension sags
issues.sym: The rear of the car sits low, especially after being parked, or the air compressor runs often.
issues.why: On cars with rear air suspension, the rubber air springs crack and leak with age.
issues.next: Replace the leaking air springs, or have a shop install a coil spring conversion kit, which many owners choose.

issues.t: Squealing or chirping from the belt idler or tensioner
issues.sym: A squeal, chirp or rattle from the front of the engine, especially at startup.
issues.why: The bearings in the belt idler pulley and tensioner wear out.
issues.next: Have the pulleys spun by hand to find the noisy one. Replace it along with the belt if the belt is worn.

issues.t: Alternator failure
issues.sym: A battery or charging light, dim lights, a dead battery, or stalling in traffic.
issues.why: The alternator wears out with mileage, and owners report replacing it on many cars.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. A failing alternator can leave you stranded, so replace it soon.

issues.t: Headlights suddenly go out (recall)
issues.sym: The headlights shut off by themselves while driving, sometimes coming back on after flicking the switch.
issues.why: The lighting control module can fail and cut power to the headlights. This is the most-reported Grand Marquis problem on RepairPal and led to recall 15V-861.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-861. Have it fixed right away, since losing headlights at night is dangerous.

issues.t: Rusted steering shaft can cause loss of steering (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk in the steering, loose steering, or the steering wheel suddenly not turning the wheels.
issues.why: In salt-belt states the lower steering column bearing can corrode and separate, which can cause a loss of steering. Ford recalled these cars under 13V-385, and later recalled some cars again under 14V-704 because the upper intermediate shaft was not repaired correctly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls 13V-385 and 14V-704. If the steering feels odd, do not drive the car.

issues.t: Cruise control switch can start an underhood fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the brake master cylinder area, sometimes even with the car parked and off.
issues.why: The cruise control deactivation switch can leak brake fluid internally and overheat. Ford recalled it under 07V-336 and added a fused jumper under 08V-051.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for both recalls. Park outside, away from buildings, until the repair is done.

issues.t: Battery cable can overheat and cause a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: The positive battery cable could suffer heat damage, which could lead to a fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recall 05V-518 and have the cable checked or replaced.

issues.t: Front wheel hub can fracture (recall)
issues.sym: Noise or looseness at a front wheel, or a wheel that feels like it is wobbling.
issues.why: On some cars a front hub could crack and separate from the knuckle, leaving the wheel held only by the brake caliper.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 07V-270. Stop driving if a front wheel feels loose.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop with no warning.
issues.why: The wiper control module could fail on some cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 00V-138 and have the dealer replace the module.

issues.t: Seat belt may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: There may be no warning signs.
issues.why: A small number of cars got seat belt assemblies that might not restrain an occupant properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 00V-157.

issues.t: Wrong jacking instructions (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; the risk is when using the jack to change a tire.
issues.why: The jacking instructions supplied with the car could lead to the car slipping off the jack.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 00V-200 and never put any part of your body under a car held up only by the jack.
